changes.old: U.S. clients that do not have their own VisaNet Access Point (VAP) endpoint (that decide to settle for themselves) are billed a monthly charge for funds transfers. The charge is intended to offset the added expense for Visa to send settlement wires to those that want to settle directly with Visa. The monthly charge is billed through the Billing Statement. There is no charge for the primary VisaNet funds transfer point (usually the VAP-connected processor if the processor is a funds transfer point). Clients that settle for themselves should also expect to receive wire charges from their settlement banks. All U.S. clients are billed monthly for nonfinancial transaction processing charges, which include a charge for each report generation record and for each item of clients settlement data. These charges also apply to report generation records and each item of client settlement data for any summary-level settlement reporting entities (SREs) that the client establishes. See Visa U.S.A. Inc. Operating Regulations, Volume 1— 1—General Rules

text_a: Processors that want to distribute VisaNet Settlement Service (VSS) reports directly to clients can have the acquiring or issuing identifier identified in their report records. When this option is selected, the acquiring or issuing identifier of the lowest-level SRE is placed in the Destination Identifier field of the machine-readable (TC 46) and print-ready (TC 47) report records. This destination identifier identifies the report records of the client that owns the acquiring or issuing identifier. Reports are grouped under the acquiring or issuing identifier. The Edit Package strips the header information from reports, which includes the Destination Identifier field on print-ready (TC 47) records. Processors that choose the Destination Identifier field to facilitate report distribution must pull the TC 47 records from the original delivery file (ITF). If the acquiring or issuing identifier identification option is not used, the processor identifier is placed in the Destination Identifier field. The processor is always in the report records for summary-level SREs. The acquiring or issuing identifier identification option can be used to affect the sequence that report records are received. If the acquiring or issuing identifier is identified in report records, the records are received in acquiring or issuing identifier sequence.
